mentl/f429c28:
Nothing on the board counted a thread. That is why judge_window = 1 could
sit beside a spawn-per-branch for ten days with every gate green
(Hβ.infer.serialized-judge-still-spawns): 433 distinct OS threads on
`fn main() = 7`, wasi_thread_start at 48.45% inclusive, roughly half the
compile spent creating and joining threads that ran strictly one at a time.
The memory that defect cost got a ratchet at the time. The threads did not.

tools/thread-gate.sh, three legs:

CONTROL — compiles and runs the frontier's real-spawn fixture and REQUIRES
its thread count above the floor. Without it a counter that reads zero
because it is blind passes forever while the defect walks through. The
first draft of this leg was exactly that: the fixture failed to compile,
wat2wasm assembled the empty output, the run exited 0, and it "passed"
having measured nothing. It now asserts the WAT byte count.

RATCHET — guest spawns scale with layer-branch count and wasmtime's own
host threads do not, so the gate reads a DELTA between a 61-declaration
program and a 1-declaration one. Host overhead cancels; per-branch spawning
cannot hide in it. An absolute ceiling would have been a ratchet on the
runner's implementation detail, red on an upgrade that changed nothing
about us. Measured: 5 clones at 1 decl, 5 at 61, delta 0.
judge_spawn_delta_max: 0, seen RED at ceiling -1 before it was trusted.

DETERMINISM — two draws of one source, byte-compared. This is the leg that
survives Phase 9.2 unchanged. A race in the judge has exactly one symptom,
run-to-run variance, and it is the symptom that hid the 2026-08-07 garbled
cell: the judgment streams agreed while the emit differed, so anything
coarser than a byte compare reported agreement. Cheap enough to run every
time, which is the point — a determinism check you run only once you
already suspect a race confirms suspicions instead of raising them.

Ultimate-form-in-full (Thread 1). The e-graph gains:
- CONST-FOLDING (lit op lit ≡ lit) — the one rule that MINTS a node: the folded
  literal is registered in the program weave AND type-bound to Int (saturate
  runs post-inference, so an un-bound new node would be NFree at lower time).
  Div/mod by zero does not fold — the trap is the program's meaning.

GraphWrite threads through the saturation chain (const-fold mints nodes);
const-fold is tried first (lit-op-lit only), the identities match var-involving
forms — disjoint, so the pass short-circuits to the one rule that fires.

Gate-green: seed builds, micros 5/5 (const-fold doesn't fire on their
var-arithmetic, so untouched), census 184 (shadow). End-to-end WAT verification
of the fold is blocked by a PRE-EXISTING mentl2 inference gap (`fn main() = 7`

mentl/f4a0f94:
Audit caught a truth-discard in infer_walk_stmt tag-129 dispatch
(introduced in the Stage 2B commit 8d0b8ec): returning empty without
binding the stmt's handle to NErrorHole was throwing away the Reason
chain — the stmt's handle would stay NFree, $lookup_ty wouldn't see
the parse-error truth, the Why Engine couldn't walk it.

Fixed: bind the stmt's handle to NErrorHole(reason) at the graph
layer, matching the expr-side substrate (NErrorExpr tag 102 already
bound correctly in Stage 2B). Now both NErrorStmt and NErrorExpr
preserve the Reason chain through the full pipeline:

  parser → sentinel-AST tag (102/129) + handle + span
  infer  → graph_bind_kind(handle, NErrorHole(reason))    ← truth preserved
  lower  → LConst-0 carrying handle forward
  emit   → emit_lconst reads $lookup_ty(handle) → NErrorHole
           → TError-hole (114) → emits (unreachable)
  Why    → Reason chain stays in graph; walks back to span

Per protocol_emit_is_graph_projection.md + protocol_cursor_is_the_substrate.md:
emit reads the graph's truth via $lookup_ty rather than fabricating
shared scratch state. The "imperative subsystem" never appears in
correct Mentl substrate; tag-102/129 dispatches read what infer wrote.

Empirical: zero output diff (185,576b on src/lower.mn pre/post),
zero stderr line count change (908). The fix doesn't alter emitted
output for the L1 path — it ensures the Reason chain is reachable
from any future Why-engine walk + LSP hover + Mentl projection.

turbosort/f49b4c7:
The radix core zeroed a fixed [[usize; 8*256]; 4] histogram (64 KiB) on
every call regardless of key width and input size, and allocated a fully
zeroed scratch Vec. Rework the core so histograms are sized to the key's
actual pass count, computed with a single copy below 8K elements and four
interleaved copies above, and scatter into uninitialized spare capacity
(Vec::with_capacity, never zeroed) since every pass writes all positions.
The 4K u32 tier is about 2.5x faster.

Add a wide-digit path for 8-byte keys at 64K+ elements: 11-bit digits in
six passes instead of eight byte passes, which cut 1M-element u64 by 1.4x
over the byte path. 8-, 13-, and 16-bit widths were benchmarked and lost;
the constants record why. One-byte keys now use a counting sort with no
scratch buffer, and all radix entry points detect already-sorted input in
one scan and return early.

sort_with_buffer keeps its no-allocation contract: 8-byte keys stay on
the byte-digit path there rather than taking the heap-allocating wide
path, gated by a const parameter that only sort() sets.
two-top/f449e85:
Until now the android matrix target only built fixed_math because
bevy_internal force-pulls bevy_android under cfg(target_os="android"),
and bevy_android depends on android-activity = "0.6" without
enabling either of its mutually-exclusive game-activity /
native-activity features. android-activity then emits
compile_error!() and the whole graph fails to build for
aarch64-linux-android. fixed_math escaped only because it has no
bevy dep at all.

crates/sim/Cargo.toml:
  * Adds android-activity = { version = "0.6", features = [
    "game-activity"] } as a target.'cfg(target_os = "android")'.
    dependencies entry. game-activity is the modern path (Java-side
    GameActivity); native-activity is legacy NativeActivity. Cargo
    union-merges the feature with bevy_android's transitive dep,
    so the compile_error stops firing across the whole sim graph.
    Strict no-op on every non-android target.
  * Cargo.lock picks up the new dep + its transitive simd_cesu8.

.github/workflows/determinism.yml:
  * aarch64-linux-android matrix entry: pkg-args goes from
    `-p fixed_math` to `--workspace --exclude app`. sim/replay/
    render/sync_test/replay_sync now compile for android, which is
    the property the matrix has always wanted to gate on; app is
    still its own bevy_winit + wgpu cross-build packaging story
    that Phase 7.5 cycle 3 (cargo-apk + SIDELOAD.md) will handle.
  * Split the run step: non-android targets continue to nextest run;
    android does `cargo build --target ... --tests --locked`.
    GitHub-hosted ubuntu runners can cross-compile to aarch64-android
    but can't execute the resulting binaries — cargo build --tests
    exercises every test target's compilation, which is what we
    actually need to gate on.

Verified locally: cargo nextest run --workspace --locked passes
74/74 (TMPDIR redirected to target/test_tmp due to a saturated
local tmpfs); cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings
clean. Cross-platform android build verified by CI.

noodles/f405c09:
The park armed only via wakeContext and stop(), on the assumption
that a fresh context sits suspended until the first gesture. On an
installed PWA with high media engagement Chrome auto-starts the
context at page load, so a freshly opened noodles burned the whole
graph's audio CPU - five compressors, chorus, LFOs, the master
stack - while sitting untouched on the session grid. The builder
caught it reading aud x1.0x on the overlay, idle after boot, on a
23 percent battery. One call arms the park before the API returns;
receipt (.tmp/dbg-boot-park.mjs, autoplay-allowed headless run):
state running at load, suspended by 7 s. The first tap still wakes
it synchronously; nothing about the sound changes - suspended is
bit-identical silence.
